\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{કરાર} (karār)}{કરાર (karār)}]{\gu{કરાર} (karār) — a contract}

\label{lesson:GU-C350-karar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for neutral, then the Gujarati for to behave.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{કરાર}}
\textbf{\gu{કરાર}} — \emph{karār} — \textquotedblleft{}a contract\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{બંને} \gu{વેપારીઓએ} \gu{એક} \gu{કરાર} \gu{પર} \gu{સહી} \gu{કરી}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{banne vepārīoe ek karār par sahī karī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Both merchants signed a contract.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{કરાર}} (\emph{karār}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{qarār}, \textquotedblleft{}firmness, a settlement\textquotedblright{}, through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{karār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{karār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{banne vepārīoe ek karār par sahī karī.} — Both merchants signed a contract.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for neutral, then the Gujarati for to behave, then say \emph{karār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{કરાર} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A contract\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{દસ્તાવેજ} (dastāvej)}{દસ્તાવેજ (dastāvej)}]{\gu{દસ્તાવેજ} (dastāvej) — a document}

\label{lesson:GU-C350-dastavej}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to behave, then the Gujarati for a contract.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{દસ્તાવેજ}}
\textbf{\gu{દસ્તાવેજ}} — \emph{dastāvej} — \textquotedblleft{}a document\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{મિલકતના} \gu{બધા} \gu{દસ્તાવેજ} \gu{સાચવીને} \gu{રાખો}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{milkatnā badhā dastāvej sācvīne rākho.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Keep all the property documents safe.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{દસ્તાવેજ}} (\emph{dastāvej}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{dastāvez}, \textquotedblleft{}a document, a deed\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{મુક્ત} (mukt)}{મુક્ત (mukt)}]{\gu{મુક્ત} (mukt) — free of; released (from a duty, a debt or a worry)}

\label{lesson:GU-C350-mukt}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a contract, then the Gujarati for a document.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{મુક્ત}}
\textbf{\gu{મુક્ત}} — \emph{mukt} — \textquotedblleft{}free of; released (from a duty, a debt or a worry)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{બધું} \gu{બિલ} \gu{ચૂકવ્યા} \gu{પછી} \gu{તે} \gu{ચિંતાથી} \gu{મુક્ત} \gu{થયો}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{badhũ bil cūkavyā pachī te cintāthī mukt thayo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Once he had paid the whole bill he was free of worry.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{મુક્ત}} (\emph{mukt}) is a tatsama, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{mukta}, \textquotedblleft{}loosened, set free\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mukt}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{badhũ bil cūkavyā pachī te cintāthī mukt thayo.} — Once he had paid the whole bill he was free of worry.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a contract, then the Gujarati for a document, then say \emph{mukt} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{જપ્ત} (japt)}{જપ્ત (japt)}]{\gu{જપ્ત} (japt) — seized (by the authorities)}

\label{lesson:GU-C350-japt}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a document, then the Gujarati for free of.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{જપ્ત}}
\textbf{\gu{જપ્ત}} — \emph{japt} — \textquotedblleft{}seized (by the authorities)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{પોલીસે} \gu{નકલી} \gu{માલ} \gu{જપ્ત} \gu{કર્યો}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{polīse naklī māl japt karyo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police seized the fake goods.
\end{quote}

\textbf{\gu{જપ્ત}} (\emph{japt}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ẓabt}, \textquotedblleft{}seizure, control\textquotedblright{}, through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{વસૂલવું} (vasūlvũ)}{વસૂલવું (vasūlvũ)}]{\gu{વસૂલવું} (vasūlvũ) — to recover a debt; to collect money owed}

\label{lesson:GU-C350-vasulvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for free of, then the Gujarati for seized.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{વસૂલવું}}
\textbf{\gu{વસૂલવું}} — \emph{vasūlvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to recover a debt; to collect money owed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{બેંક} \gu{બાકી} \gu{રકમ} \gu{વ્યાજ} \gu{સાથે} \gu{વસૂલશે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{beṅk bākī rakam vyāj sāthe vasūlśe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bank will recover the outstanding amount with interest.
\end{quote}

Past, with \gu{તેણે} (he or she …): \gu{તેણે} \gu{બધી} \gu{રકમ} \gu{વસૂલી}, \emph{teṇe badhī rakam vasūlī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{વસૂલવું}} (\emph{vasūlvũ}) is built on \emph{vasūl}, \textquotedblleft{}recovered, received\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{wuṣūl}, \textquotedblleft{}arrival, receipt\textquotedblright{}, through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for free of, then the Gujarati for seized, then say \emph{vasūlvũ} again
\end{itemize}
